short_summary: Repo-aware IDE copilot vendor evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private for EU-resident vector indexes. Needs sub-100ms token streaming, per-repo chunking presets, deterministic model pinning for reproducible completions, and CI-triggered incremental embedding updates.
notes:
Context: RepoForge AI builds a repo-aware code assistant integrated into developer IDEs. Primary ask: reliable retrieval from private monorepos with EU residency for embeddings and vector index.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-02-25: Intro demo with AE/SE; demoed streaming examples and retrieval pipeline. Customer emphasized deterministic outputs for release parity.
- 2026-02-28: SE architecture session 1min2  discussed chunking heuristics (language-aware vs file-bound), index-time vs query-time embedding strategies, and preferred vector DBs (Qdrant managed or on-prem Milvus). Action: SE to propose config examples.
- 2026-03-03: Security questionnaire submitted; customer requested KMS/HSM integration details and deletion controls tied to commit hashes.
- 2026-03-07: Pricing and capacity planning call; requested Dedicated pool with reserved concurrent stream slots and a fallback policy spec for capacity saturation.

Requirements (bullet):
- Workload: IDE copilot (short-form completions) + repo search/reranking.
- Latency targets: token-stream median <= 80ms, 95p <= 180-220ms depending on repo size. End-to-end retrieval 1-2 round trips target.
- Scale: target 200-400 concurrent active IDE sessions at peak; thousands of DAU.
- Model needs: model/version pinning for deterministic behavior; acceptance testing against golden prompts. Open to quantized models but must match GA outputs.
- Embeddings & vector DB: prefer index-time embedding pipeline with CI hooks for incremental updates. Vector DB must be EU-resident; preference: managed Qdrant in EU or on-prem Milvus/Redis Vector with KMS.
- Chunking: per-repo presets; allow larger chunk sizes for language files with dense context and sliding-window fallback for long docs.
- Caching & batching: heavy prefix cache expected; want Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization to reduce cost without increasing tail latency.

POC ask / success metrics:
- 2-week Dedicated POC in eu-central or eu-west.
- Ingest 2 large mono-repos (~80-150GB combined), run CI-simulated incremental updates.
- Measure: median token latency, 95th percentile token latency, vector query latency, retrieval top-5 recall, cost per 10k tokens, embedding throughput.
- Goal: median token latency < 100ms, retrieval top-5 recall > 85%, vector query 95p < 50ms inside VPC.

Open technical questions for Redwood:
- How is per-repo chunking configured and overridden at index time? Need example config.
- Clear doc on model fallback mapping when Dedicated capacity is saturated; customer requires deterministic fallback mapping rules.
- Can Redwood guarantee vector index deletion by commit ID and provide audit log entry for deletion?
- KMS/HSM rotation policy and proof of integration for on-prem vector DB encrypt-at-rest.

Action owners & next steps:
- AE (Maya): coordinate NDA + DPIA timeline with Legal.
- SE (Ravi): deliver POC runbook + sample chunking/embedding config by 2026-03-12.
- Solutions: provision Dedicated EU pool for POC (tentative 2026-03-20).
